data.title: Strengthening Muscle for Healthy Ageing: Innovative Treatments for Sarcopenia
data.authors: Ancel S; Le Moal E; Wang YX; Blau HM

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: A major pharma-facing review (Blau lab, Stanford/Sanford Burnham) surveying emerging drug strategies for sarcopenia — the age-related loss of muscle mass/strength with no approved therapy. Among the pleiotropic mechanisms discussed, mTORC1 inhibitors are highlighted specifically for their ability to restore impaired autophagy in aging muscle, alongside NAD-related molecules, urolithin A, myostatin inhibitors, SARMs, and 15-PGDH ('gerozyme') inhibitors. Useful high-level context for where mTORC1 modulation sits among competing anti-sarcopenia strategies, though it does not itself address dynamic/temporal mTOR activity.
data.abstract_excerpt: Millions of people worldwide suffer from sarcopenia, a clinically recognized syndrome that is defined as the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength. Sarcopenia reduces mobility, leads to falls and fractures, and increases the risk of death, posing an ever-increasing health-care and economic burden to society. There are currently no approved therapies for the syndrome, partly owing to its multifactorial aetiology, highlighting the need for therapies with pleiotropic beneficial effects on muscle function.

extracted_findings.intervention: Narrative review of pharmacological strategies for sarcopenia: mTORC1 inhibitors, NAD-related molecules, urolithin A, myostatin inhibitors, SARMs, VEGF/apelin, anti-inflammatory agents, 15-PGDH inhibitors, GLP-1RA combinations
extracted_findings.effect: Synthesizes emerging drug classes to preserve muscle mass/strength in aging; positions mTORC1 inhibition as one of several pleiotropic strategies
